rv.q: All of this was channeled by the acute awareness of conductor Ramón Tebar and this proved to be a most historical "La Bohème" to behold.
The test of any La bohème is whether it brings a tear to your eye. This one did.
Here was where De Tommaso’s mastery of nuance and Grigoryan’s dialing her voice from inmost pianissimo to full-throated longing made the text come palpably to life.
Mkhitaryan is a soulful, raven-haired Mimì, her dark-hued voice filling Puccini’s soaring vocal lines with ease and emotion.
Familiar it may be, but it never stales, particularly when in good hands (and voices).

cn.t: The Met's La Bohème earns strong reviews, with critics praising standout tenor Freddie De Tommaso's last-minute heroics as Rodolfo and the soulful performances in Zeffirelli's refurbished production.

vr.q: if you are someone that doesn't like the current trend of minimalism on Broadway, go see La Boheme at the met.
